name: 2R spherical shoulder + C-ring axial bearing on the upper arm
topology: scapula base -> R1 hub (axis through GH, on top/back of the shoulder) -> link -> R2 hub (axis through GH) -> link to an open C-ring thin-section bearing (axis = humerus long axis) around the upper arm just below the deltoid insertion -> user's upper-arm cuff; passive self-aligning slide (along the humerus) between ring and cuff
dof_reasoning: R1, R2 set the humerus direction (2 DOF), the C-ring sets axial rotation (1 DOF) = 3 active; the passive slide along the humerus is set by the chain closure with the cuff (absorbs GH translation along the arm).
description: Only two hubs over the shoulder; the axial-rotation joint becomes a low ring hugging the arm where the skin is stable (mid upper arm), so link 2 only has to reach the ring, not wrap the deltoid.
model_spec: R1 axis u1 fixed in the scapula frame S through GH; R2 axis u2 rotates about u1, through GH; humerus direction d from frame H; solve the 2R spherical IK for d (two branches, keep continuity); links as 8x3 mm straps on great-circle arcs at radius r_link (skin radius along the arc + clearance); C-ring: torus section 6 mm radial x 8 mm axial, inner radius = upper-arm skin radius at that level + 3 mm, opening of 90-120 deg (on the medial side, toward the body); its frame follows H with the axial angle = the arm's axial rotation; link 2 attaches to the ring carriage; hubs 20 mm dia x 12 mm stack.
sweep_params: u1 direction (az, el in S), arc a1, ring level along the humerus (60-140 mm from GH), ring opening direction, link clearance 3-6 mm, branch.

name: Three concentric arc rails about the GH centre (no hubs)
topology: scapula base -> curved rail 1 (circular arc centred on GH, lying on the back/top of the shoulder) with carriage -> curved rail 2 (meridian arc centred on GH, carried by carriage 1) -> carriage 2 -> open C-ring rail around the upper arm (axial rotation) -> cuff; passive slide at the cuff
dof_reasoning: each rail is a revolute joint with a remote axis through GH (carriage position = joint angle): 3 active; the cuff slide is set by closure.
description: Replace every hub by a curved guide rail lying on the skin at constant radius from GH; nothing stands up 12 mm off the skin; rails overlap the shoulder like a spherical cage.
model_spec: rail 1: arc of radius R1 (skin radius + 4 mm) in a plane whose normal u1 is fixed in S; carriage 1 (20x12x8 mm block) at angle q1 along it; rail 2: arc of radius R2 in a plane containing GH, carried by carriage 1 with normal perpendicular to u1, carriage 2 at angle q2; rail section 8 x 4 mm; solve q1, q2 so carriage 2 sits on the humerus direction line's great circle that the C-ring needs; C-ring as in seed-2r-cring; rail lengths limit the range (a carriage beyond its rail = pose not taken).
sweep_params: u1, rail 1 length (deg), rail 2 length, radii offsets, C-ring level.

name: Low-profile spherical parallel 3-RRR wrapped around the shoulder
topology: scapula base plate carries 3 active R joints (axes through GH) at 3 spots around the shoulder (back, top, front); each leg: proximal arc link -> passive R (axis through GH) -> distal arc link -> passive R on a moving 'platform' ring around the upper arm (axes through GH)
dof_reasoning: an Agile-Eye-type 3-RRR spherical parallel mechanism: 3 actuated base joints, 6 passive joints all fully set by the loop closures (no undriven spare coordinate). FLAG: 6 passive joints - the user rules on whether many passive joints are acceptable.
description: Spreads the load over three short legs that each stay close to their own patch of skin instead of one long serial chain over the whole shoulder; singularities can be placed outside the range.
model_spec: unit vectors u_i (base axes, fixed in S), w_i (intermediate axes), v_i (platform axes, fixed in a platform frame attached to H); IK: given platform orientation (from H), v_i known; solve w_i as the intersection of two cones (angle a1 from u_i, a2 from v_i) - 2 branches per leg, keep continuity; links: 8x3 mm straps on the great-circle arcs u_i->w_i and w_i->v_i at radius = skin + clearance; 9 hubs (20 mm, 12 mm stack); check leg-leg collision and the singular configurations (pose not taken when the Jacobian condition number > 50).
sweep_params: base axes placement (3 directions), platform axes placement, arc angles a1, a2, branch per leg, platform ring level.

name: Base yaw + double-parallelogram remote-centre elevation + arm ring
topology: scapula base -> R1 (axis through GH, roughly vertical-ish in S) -> planar double parallelogram (all 5-6 joints parallel, its remote centre of motion at GH) giving elevation in the plane set by R1 -> C-ring axial bearing on the upper arm -> cuff; passive slide at the cuff
dof_reasoning: R1 + the parallelogram's single DOF (elevation) + the ring = 3 active; the parallelogram's other joints are set by its loop closures.
description: Surgical-robot RCM idea: the parallelogram puts the virtual elevation axis at GH while its bars run along the skin behind the shoulder.
model_spec: R1 rotates the parallelogram plane about u1 through GH; inside the plane, a double parallelogram with bar lengths L1, L2 and offset h places its output bar so it rotates about GH; bars 8x4 mm, joints 14 mm dia x 8 mm; output bar to the C-ring; solve the elevation from the humerus direction projected into the plane (and R1 from the plane orientation); the bars sweep a region behind/above the shoulder - check skin contact.
sweep_params: u1, parallelogram plane orientation offset, L1, L2, h, ring level.

name: Non-spherical offset 3R with passive self-aligning slides
topology: scapula base -> R1 (axis offset 10-30 mm from GH) -> R2 (offset) -> R3 (axis near the humerus axis) -> passive 2-DOF self-aligning slide pair (prismatic along and across the humerus) -> cuff
dof_reasoning: 3 active revolutes; the 2 passive slides absorb the mismatch between the non-concurrent axes and the GH rotation plus GH translation; they are set by closure with the cuff (the arm drives them).
description: Drop the requirement that all axes meet at GH: offset axes let links lie flat on the skin; the passive slides make up the difference.
model_spec: DH-like chain from S with axis points p_i and directions u_i; given the cuff pose (from H), solve q1..q3 and the slide values s1, s2 by least squares with bounds (slides +-15 mm); pose not taken if residual > 0.5 mm or a slide hits its bound; links 8x3 mm straps following the skin between axis points; hubs 20x12 mm; slide carriage 20x10x8 mm.
sweep_params: axis offsets and directions (6-9 params, keep coarse), slide ranges.

name: Nested sliding shells (pauldron) + arm ring
topology: scapula base shell -> shell 1 (spherical cap segment centred on GH, sliding over the base shell about axis u1) -> shell 2 (sliding over shell 1 about axis u2, both through GH) -> C-ring axial bearing on the arm -> cuff
dof_reasoning: two shell-on-shell revolute slides about axes through GH + the ring = 3 active; cuff slide passive by closure.
description: Metal as thin overlapping spherical shells over the deltoid like armour lames; the joints are the large-diameter sliding interfaces (iglidur liners), so the metal sits close to the skin everywhere.
model_spec: shells as spherical-cap patches of radius R = skin radius at that region + clearance (t = 2 mm shell + 1 mm liner), angular extents as parameters; shell i rotates about u_i through GH; patches must not penetrate the skin in any pose - the deltoid bulges, so check with the bench; the stack of 2-3 overlapping shells adds 3 mm each; ring as in seed-2r-cring.
sweep_params: u1, u2, shell angular extents, radius offsets, ring level.

name: Trombone arc: one curved slide through a swivel guide on top of the scapula
topology: S (scapula base on the user's handler) -> J1: swivel about b (S-fixed axis through GH). It is a thin-section ring (KAA15XL0 class, O38 bore) on the S-top skin, and its upper race carries the guide. L1 = the guide: 4 preloaded needle cam-follower pairs. -> J2: rotation about p2. It is a Ti arc on L2, a circle about p2 at polar angle A1 that passes through b, sliding through the guide. No metal sits at p2's pierce point. -> L2 = arc + short connector -> J3: O20 v5 hub about W on the lateral deltoid (W is humerus-fixed, ~19 deg below the GH level). Its lower plate is on the arm-side BOTTOM stub. -> H. Active: J1, J2, J3. Passive: none. The user's cuff liner and the optional self-aligning cuff slides stay outside the count.
dof_reasoning: Kinematically this is a spherical 3R with axes b, p2 and W, all through GH. S->L1 rotates about b. The arc is a circle about p2, and p2 is fixed in both L1 (guide) and L2 (arc), so sliding the arc through the guide is exactly a rotation about p2. L2->H rotates about W. The arm orientation fixes W in S. p2 then follows from the two-circle closure (angle A1 to b, angle A2 to W) on one branch. So the swivel angle, the arc position and the hub angle are all unique functions of the arm pose. No spare coordinate exists and nothing can sag. The guide rollers, the arc slide and the arc position are one coordinate (theta2).
description: A single 10 mm wide Ti band, bent to a circle about a virtual axis. It runs from a hub on the lateral deltoid up over the shoulder and through a swivelling guide on top of the scapula (supraspinatus/acromion region, where the baseline base hub is already 82 % in band). Past the guide, the free end of the band sticks out on the side away from the arm, like a trombone slide. REST (sep b-W ~90-110 deg): the guide sits near the far end of the arc. The band lies from the deltoid hub over the acromion to the top, with 10-30 deg of tail over the medial-posterior top. OVERHEAD (sep ~40 deg): W comes up to ~40 deg from the guide and the band slides out. Its tail (up to ~90 deg of arc, ~90 mm) lies over the trapezius toward the base of the neck/upper back. Only a short piece sits between the guide and the arm. ACROSS-BODY: J1 swivels forward. The band runs from the top over the front of the shoulder to the hub; the tail lies posterior over the top of the scapula. BEHIND-BACK (reach back pocket, sep ~110-117 deg): the band runs from the top down over the posterior deltoid. The tail is short and points anterior over the clavicle region (S-frame skin r 41-53 mm there). Metal near the skin: the guide + J1 ring at the S-top (~14 mm stack, only under the guide); the band at a constant 56-60 mm from GH over skin of 44-60 mm; the J3 hub on the arm. Design rule found while screening (geometric argument, not yet measured on the bench): a rail may continue past its sliding contact only on the side away from the arm. At R~55 mm the arm fills a cone of ~60-65 deg about its axis (humerus-frame skin map). An arc fixed to L1, or an S-fixed rail crossing an arm ring (a 'turret'), therefore runs into the arm. So the arc belongs on the arm-side member and the guide on the scapula side.
why_better: It removes the baseline's two worst zones at once. (1) The J2 hub zone: 18.5 % of the covered skin and 0.7 % in band. On the champion, p2 comes within 47 deg of the arm on the clips and 11 deg on the workspace, and the hub sweeps skin 58-93 mm from GH. (2) The two link ribbons: 27.8 % of the covered skin, ~20 % in band combined. In their place is one thin band along the b->W path, with no metal at p2. The kinematics stay the champion's (two-circle closure on 100 % of clip frames and 96 % of workspace poses with a 5 deg margin), so the bench isolates the effect of the realisation. It also opens kinematic space that the hub-based GPU search cannot use: p2 may point anywhere, even under the trunk skin, because nothing is built there. Stack: a 4 mm band + 2 mm gap, against a 12.25 mm hub + 3 mm plates. Why W stays lateral instead of a humeral-axis collar: with W along the humerus and the J1 element on the scapula, the best S axis keeps the hub 69 deg from the arm but brings its antipode within 29 deg (clips; 28/11 deg on the workspace). That is near-singular, and the collar twist winds ~300 deg (computed on the bench poses).
main_risk: (1) The tail: when the arm is overhead, up to ~90 mm of band sticks out past the guide (130 deg of arc over the workspace range), and it may reach the neck/head or upper back. A 2-stage telescoping arc halves it. (2) Constant radius: every point of the band is R_a from GH, while the skin under it runs from ~44 mm (top) to ~60 mm (deltoid), so parts of the band sit 12-16 mm out. (3) Near W, the band's circle about p2 may pass inside the arm cone in poses where p2 swings close to the arm (the champion's p2 comes within 11 deg of the arm on the workspace). (4) A ~100 deg open arc cantilevered from W: twist/stiffness (FINDINGS: a 24x4 Ti band twists ~5 deg at 25 N.m over 75 mm, so ~2 deg at 10 N.m). The stack under the guide is ~14 mm. A rolling guide on a Ti band needs hardened race strips.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: pure 3R closure, unique on the branch, with rolling bearings throughout: thin-section ring at J1, needle cam followers on hardened strips along the band edges, O20 v5 preloaded pair at J3. No spare and no stall. The band is ~18 g (10x4 Ti, ~100 mm) and the guide ~25 g. MVP2 drive: J1 by a cable around the ring housing OD (r ~26 mm). J2 by a cable anchored at both band ends in a groove on the band top, wrapped once round a capstan in the guide (the band is its own drum, r = R_a sin A1 ~55 mm, so tension stays low). J3 by a drum on the hub. Sensing: J1 and J3 by magnet + hall as in the v5 hub; J2 by a magnetic pole strip along the band, read by a hall array in the guide.
model_spec:
C (shared): sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); import concept_bench as CB, body_pose as BP; B = CB.Bench(); RH = np.array(BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']). Per pose i: Rs = B.frames(i)['S'][0], Rh = B.frames(i)['H'][0], HG = Rs.T @ Rh @ RH. HG is the humerus in scapula frame S with canonical axes: humerus -y, lateral +z, anterior +x at plane=elev=axial=0 (checked: Rh@RH = rot(y,plane) rot(x,-elev) rot(y,axial)). An S point x maps to thorax Rs@x; a canonical-humerus point y maps to Rs@HG@y. GH is the origin and there are no translations. bvec(az,el) = (-cos el cos az, sin el, cos el sin az). wdir(d,az) = (sin d sin az, -cos d, sin d cos az). circ_int(c1,r1,c2,r2,sign) = band_impl.py line 892. rot(u,a) = Rodrigues. r_skin(i,u) = distance from GH to the outermost posed skin along thorax unit u (Moller-Trumbore against B.skin(i) faces with |v| < 170 mm, or bisection on B.dist). Envelope fit, 2 passes: pass 1 runs the IK on the fit-clip poses (B.kind=='clip') and stores, per metal sample expressed in its member's frame, the max r_skin along it. Pass 2 sets the skin side at that max + 2 mm; a constant-radius part uses the max over all its samples + 2. Champion (cad_r18_n3_s1392_1_f300): b = bvec(32.55,80.56) = (-0.138,0.986,0.088); W0 = wdir(71.38,4.78) = (0.079,-0.319,0.944); A1 77.41 deg; A2 81.45 deg; branch -1. On the bench, sep = angle(b, HG W0) is 39.5-116.8 deg (clips) and 8-158 deg (ws); angle(b, arm) >= 88.7 deg (clips) and >= 67.6 deg (ws). O20 v5 hub keep-out: disk r 10 mm, 12.25 mm from its lower skin face to the crown, lower plate 3 mm. Strap: 14 x 3 mm Ti. Sample skin-facing and top faces at ~1 pt / 4 mm2. BOTTOM stub (the same in every concept that ends at an arm hub): a 14 x 6 mm strap from the J3 lower plate 40 mm down the lateral arm, skin side at envelope + 2.
IK per pose: W = HG@W0; p2 = circ_int(b, A1, W, A2, -1). Not taken if there is no intersection or sep is outside [|A1-A2|+5, A1+A2-5] deg.
L2 frame: e1 = p2; e2 = normalize(W - (W.p2) p2); e3 = e1 x e2. Guide azimuth phi_g = atan2(b.e3, b.e2); on the champion it is 40-120 deg (clips) and 7-173 deg (ws).
ARC (on L2): centreline c(phi) = cos A1 e1 + sin A1 (cos phi e2 + sin phi e3), for phi in [phi_lo, phi_hi] = [min phi_g - 12, max phi_g + 12] over the fit clips (~[28, 132] deg, ~103 mm at R 58). Band 10 mm wide (polar A1 +- 5/R_a rad about p2) x 4 mm radial, at radii [R_a, R_a+4]. R_a = envelope max over the band + 2 (expect 56-60 mm).
J1 + GUIDE (on L1, at b): the J1 ring (KAA15XL0 38.1x47.6x4.76 in housings) is an annulus about b, at 19-26 mm from the b axis, axial span [z1, z1+6] along b. z1 = envelope max of the skin's axial height under the annulus + 2. The guide is a keep-out box centred at R_a*b: 30 mm along the arc tangent t = -sin(phi_g) e2 + cos(phi_g) e3, 22 mm across along m = normalize(p2 - (p2.b) b), and radial [R_a-3, R_a+7] along b. Enforce R_a >= z1 + 9 (raise R_a if needed).
CONNECTOR (on L2): strap from c(phi_lo) to the J3 upper plate along the great circle, with its radius ramped linearly from R_a to R_W + 9.
J3: O20 v5 hub on W. Its arm-side skin face R_W = envelope max within 12 mm of W (canonical frame) + 2; stack [R_W, R_W+12.25]. Plus the BOTTOM stub.
NOT TAKEN: closure fails; phi_g outside [phi_lo+12, phi_hi-12] (guide past an arc end); any sample < 0 mm (bench contact). Also report the tail length (phi_hi - phi_g) per pose and the min distance of the tail to the neck/head in overhead poses.
VARIANT to run as well: a 2-stage telescoping arc. The outer stage spans half the range in a sleeve, and its midpoint is held by one scissor X, which halves the tail.
GH translation: none on the bench, because S rotates about GH. In use, the user's liner and the optional passive cuff slides take it, as for the baseline.
sweep_params: Arc range source: fit clips [28,132] vs clips + workspace p5-p95 [26,164] deg. R_a offset 0..+4 mm over the envelope. J1 realisation: O38 thin ring vs O20 v5 hub. J3 realisation: hub vs O38 ring. Axes around the champion: b az 0-60 / el 60-90; W0 delta 55-85 / az -20..30; A1, A2 60-95 deg; branch +-1. Telescoping arc on/off. Band width 8-12 mm.
prior_art: Circular-guided RCM for surgical robots (Yip et al., ROBIO 2014: an arc slides through a carriage, centred on the RCM). CADEN-7 and MEDARM curved tracks (fixed tracks, not an arc sliding through a swivel). No shoulder exo is known with an arm-side arc sliding through a swivel on the scapula.

name: Annular-ring 3R: open-bore thin-section rings at every joint axis
topology: S -> J1: thin-section 4-point ring (KAA15XL0, 38.1x47.6x4.76) centred on b's pierce point; lower race on the base, upper race on L1 -> L1 strap, attached at the ring rims -> J2: the same ring type about p2 -> L2 strap -> J3: the same ring type about W; lower race on the arm-side plate (BOTTOM stub) -> H. No metal inside the O38 bores. Active: J1, J2, J3. Passive: none.
dof_reasoning: This is the champion's spherical 3R, with each revolute realised as a large-bore ring bearing coaxial with its joint axis (through GH). The three ring angles are the three joint angles. The arm sets them uniquely through the two-circle closure on one branch. There is no passive element.
description: The baseline's joint layout, but each 12.25 mm O20 hub becomes a flat annulus, 8 mm thick and ~O38-56 mm across. Its open bore surrounds the axis pierce point, so the skin dome rises into the hole instead of lifting a solid hub; the links leave from the ring rims. REST: the J1 ring sits around the top of the shoulder with the acromion/supraspinatus apex inside the bore. The J2 ring sits wherever p2 is, on the posterior-superior shoulder in most poses. The J3 ring sits on the lateral deltoid ~19 deg below the GH level. OVERHEAD: the J2 ring travels onto the back over the medial scapula. The champion's J2 hub went under the trunk skin there; the bore lets that bulge through. ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: as on the champion, J2 swings anterior-superior / posterior, and the links run over the front / back of the shoulder. On a dome of radius 44 mm, a ring of radius 19 / 25 mm sits 4.3 / 7.8 mm lower than the apex. Its 8 mm height therefore costs about as much as one hub lower plate.
why_better: A hub stands 12.25 mm proud exactly where the skin is highest, at the axis pierce point of a dome. A ring moves the metal to the dome's flanks and leaves the apex free. Targets: the champion's J2 zone (18.5 % of covered skin, 0.7 % in band, too far by a median 20.6 mm, 9.6 mm of it slack) and the JN hub zone (19.5 % of covered skin, 61 % in band). It is the cheapest test of the lens: identical kinematics, and a twin model with O20 hubs isolates the effect of the ring. FINDINGS: joint size is worth ~20 points of workspace (hub_r 8.5 vs 11.5); a hollow ring is a different way to shrink a joint's effective height. MVP2 bonus: the race OD is a cable drum of r ~24-30 mm, so 2.5x less cable tension than on an O20 hub.
main_risk: The bore only helps on a dome. On the moving J2 skin the flanks move too, and a bulge that rises above the ring plane at the rim still hits the ring. On a steep flank (35 deg at rho 25 on r 44) a flat ring lifts its outer rim. The O48-66 footprint covers more skin, and the links get shorter by the ring radii. Thin-section rings need stiff, precise Ti housings: ~18 g per ring + ~10 g of housings, ~90 g for three joints.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the same 3R as the champion, which moves freely with rolling bearings (0.05 N.m measured by judge/dynamics.py). A preloaded thin-section 4-point ring adds ~0.01-0.05 N.m. No spare. MVP2: a cable groove on each outer housing (r 24-30 mm). Sensing: a multipole magnetic ring on the rotating race read by 2 halls on the fixed race (an off-axis encoder); no magnet is needed on the axis, which stays open.
model_spec:
C (shared): sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); import concept_bench as CB, body_pose as BP; B = CB.Bench(); RH = np.array(BP._rig().L['rest_humerus']). Per pose i: Rs = B.frames(i)['S'][0], Rh = B.frames(i)['H'][0], HG = Rs.T @ Rh @ RH. HG is the humerus in scapula frame S with canonical axes: humerus -y, lateral +z, anterior +x at the zero pose. An S point x maps to thorax Rs@x; a canonical-humerus point y maps to Rs@HG@y. GH is the origin. bvec(az,el) = (-cos el cos az, sin el, cos el sin az). wdir(d,az) = (sin d sin az, -cos d, sin d cos az). circ_int = band_impl.py line 892. r_skin / B.dist as the skin probe. Envelope fit, 2 passes: pass 1 runs the IK on the fit clips and stores the max skin height per sample in its member's frame; pass 2 places the part at max + 2 mm. Champion axes: b = (-0.138,0.986,0.088), W0 = (0.079,-0.319,0.944), A1 77.41 deg, A2 81.45 deg, branch -1. Strap 14 x 3 mm Ti. Samples ~1 pt / 4 mm2. BOTTOM stub: 14 x 6 mm strap from the J3 lower plate 40 mm down the lateral arm.
IK: W = HG@W0; p2 = circ_int(b, A1, W, A2, -1). Joint axes P1 = b, P2 = p2, P3 = W (S frame). Not taken if there is no intersection or sep is outside [|A1-A2|+5, A1+A2-5].
RING k: an annulus about axis P_k. Points x = z P_k + rho (cos psi q1 + sin psi q2), with q1, q2 perpendicular to P_k; rho in [rho_i, rho_i+9] (default rho_i = 19.05); z in [z_k, z_k+8]. The lower race housing [z_k, z_k+4] belongs to the proximal member and the upper [z_k+4, z_k+8] to the distal member; at J3 the lower race is the arm side. No samples at rho < rho_i (open bore). Sample: top face, bottom face, inner and outer walls, psi every 5 deg, rho every 2 mm.
z_k (envelope): for each (rho, psi) sample, find the skin's axial coordinate on the line z -> z P_k + rho u(psi) by bisection with B.dist from z = 150 mm inward to the first crossing. z_k = max over the fit-clip poses and samples + 2 mm. The J2 ring is axisymmetric about p2, so it can be generated in S per pose directly.
LINK 1 (L1): strap from the outer rim of J1's upper race (the rim point toward P2: z1+8 along P1, plus (rho_i+9) along the great-circle tangent toward P2) to the outer rim of J2's lower race (the rim point toward P1), along the great circle. Skin side from the envelope fit along the path; ends clamped to the race faces with ramps <= 35 deg.
LINK 2 (L2): from J2's upper race rim to J3's upper race rim, built the same way. Plus the BOTTOM stub from J3's lower race.
TWIN (A/B): the same code with rho_i = 0 and an O20 v5 hub (disk r 10, 12.25 mm stack, 3 mm lower plate) at each pin, so the measured difference isolates the ring.
NOT TAKEN: closure fails or sep outside the margin; any sample < 0 mm.
GH translation: none on the bench.
sweep_params: Bore radius per joint rho_i: 10 (hub twin), 13, 19, 25, 30 mm. Ring section: 4.76 vs 6.35 mm. Which joints get rings: J2 only / J2+J3 / all. Link width 10-14 mm. Champion axes +-10 deg.
prior_art: Kaydon/RBC Reali-Slim KAA-series and IKO CRBT thin-section rings (docs/research/ring_and_shell_hardware.md section 5.2). Harmony reportedly uses IKO crossed-roller rings (unverified). No exo is known that uses the bore as skin clearance.

name: Risley turret: J1 and J2 as two overlapping rings on top of the scapula
topology: S -> J1: ring (annulus, O30-48) about b on the S-top -> L1: small plate joining J1's upper race and J2's lower race -> J2: ring about p2. With A1 only 30-45 deg, its pierce point also stays on the S-top cap. -> L2: J2's upper race + one strap down to W -> J3: O20 v5 hub (or ring) about W on the lateral deltoid -> H. Active: J1, J2, J3. Passive: none.
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R with a short first link (A1 30-45 deg, A2 65-85 deg): rotations about b, p2 and W, all through GH. The two-circle closure on one branch fixes all three angles from the arm pose. No passive element. Like a pair of Risley prisms or a tilting turntable, J1 and J2 point L2, and J3 handles the rest.
description: Everything that rotates against moving skin moves onto the stable top of the scapula. Two stacked, partly overlapping flat rings sit on the supraspinatus/acromion cap, their centres ~38 mm apart at R 55. One strap runs from the upper ring down over the lateral shoulder to the deltoid hub. REST: both rings on the top, J2 on the side of the top away from the arm; the strap runs over the acromion to the lateral deltoid. OVERHEAD (sep ~40 deg): the strap path shortens and lies over the top. J2 stays >= 90 deg from the arm (measured on every clip frame for A1 40 / A2 75). ACROSS-BODY: J1 turns the ring pair forward and the strap runs over the front of the shoulder. BEHIND-BACK: the strap runs over the posterior deltoid. S-frame skin map: the top cap (scapula-frame latitude >= 45-60 deg) has skin radius 37-54 mm with only 1-10 mm of spread between poses.
why_better: The champion's J2 pierce point comes within 47 deg of the arm on the clips and 11 deg on the workspace, and it sweeps skin 58-93 mm from GH: the single worst zone, losing 18.4 points of R1. With A1 = 40, A2 = 75, branch -1, J2 stays >= 90 deg from the arm in every clip frame (>= 41 deg on the workspace), on skin whose radius barely moves. name: Skin-stretch scissor: a tapered spherical lazy-tongs from the scapula top to the deltoid
topology: S -> J1: O20 v5 hub (or ring) about b on the S-top -> L1 = J1's upper plate, holding the scissor root (one pin + one lateral slot) -> J2: a spherical lazy-tongs of N = 4 units along the great circle b->W, every pivot axis radial through GH. Active: J1, J2 (the scissor), J3. Passive: 3N+2 = 14 scissor pivots/slots, all dependent (the lazy-tongs has mobility 1).
dof_reasoning: A spherical 3R with A1 = A2 = 90 deg. The scissor's tip frame is its root frame rotated about p2 by sigma, so the scissor is a revolute about p2 realised by telescoping. The arm sets sigma (the angle between b and HG W0), and the closure sets J1 and J3. The 14 internal joints are all functions of sigma, because a lazy-tongs is a 1-DOF linkage, so none can sag. They are passive and set by closure.
description: Instead of a rigid link that must clear every pose, a small lattice of 6 mm Ti bars stretches between the hub on top of the scapula and the deltoid hub, along the shortest path over the shoulder, the way the skin there stretches. Node k always sits at fraction k/N of the path, and each node has its own fixed radius from GH. The lattice can therefore taper from ~46 mm over the top to ~60 mm over the deltoid, and the bars stay rigid because the node radii never change. REST (sigma ~95-110 deg): stretched, ~12 mm wide, along the acromion-deltoid line. OVERHEAD (sigma ~40 deg): folded into a ~27 mm wide fan over the top of the shoulder, with no tail. ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: the lattice swings with J1 over the front / back of the shoulder top, and stretches to sigma ~117 deg behind the back. Stack: two bar layers + O8 pivot bosses = 5.5 mm.
why_better: Like the trombone, it removes the J2 hub and both link ribbons (the baseline's worst ~34 points of R1). Unlike the trombone, it has no tail and no constant-radius rail. The tapered nodes follow the skin's radius profile along the path, which a rail cannot, and the scissor always spans exactly the actual gap between the hubs. Stack 5.5 mm vs 12.25 mm + plates for a hub.
main_risk: Play and stiffness: 14 small pivots in series amplify clearance (a lazy-tongs multiplies pivot play by ~N at the tip), and the lattice is soft near full stretch. The kinematics change to A1 = A2 = 90 deg, which is singular at sigma -> 0/180; with the champion's b and W0, the workspace reaches sigma 8 and 158 deg. name: Sliding-rivet pauldron: hubless nested plates with follower-in-slot joints

description: Like the lames of a plate-armour pauldron on sliding rivets: four 2 mm Ti plates stacked over the shoulder, each at its own radius where they overlap. The S cap is innermost over the top, then L1, then the L2 band; the H saddle sits under the band's arm end. Plates can slide over each other but cannot collide there. REST: the S cap (~O50) over the supraspinatus/acromion, L1 a ~O40 disc on it, and the L2 band running from the top down over the acromion to a saddle on the lateral deltoid. name: Deltoid-strut tripod: three arc struts on the paths of the three deltoid heads (spherical 3-RPR parallel)
topology: Three legs in parallel from the scapula to an arm saddle. Leg i: S -> passive swivel about b_i: an O20 v5 hub with a guide on top, on stable scapula skin (top; anterior-medial over the clavicle/upper trapezius; posterior over the scapular spine) -> active arc slide: strut i is a Ti arc on the great circle through b_i and W_i, sliding through the guide; its angular length d_i between b_i and W_i is the active coordinate -> passive hinge about W_i: an O20 v5 hub on a humerus-fixed deltoid saddle (anterior, lateral and posterior deltoid, ~15 deg below the GH level) -> H. Active: d1, d2, d3. Passive: 6 swivels/hinges, set by closure.
dof_reasoning: The orientation of H relative to S has 3 DOF. Each strut constrains one angular distance d_i = angle(b_i, HG w_i). With 3 independent struts (Jacobian rows n_i = b_i x W_i / |.| not coplanar), the three lengths fix the arm orientation. Each leg's swivel and hinge angles then follow, because the strut body's frame is (W_i, n_i). So the 6 passive joints are all set by closure, and there is no spare.
description: Three thin curved struts run over the shoulder from scapula anchors to the arm saddle, along the paths of the deltoid's anterior, middle and posterior heads, and lengthen and shorten as those heads do. Each strut slides through a swivelling guide on its scapula anchor, and its free end sticks out past the anchor, away from the arm. REST: the middle strut runs from the acromion top down to the lateral deltoid; the anterior one from the clavicle/upper-trapezius anchor over the front of the shoulder; the posterior one from the scapular spine over the back. OVERHEAD: the arm anchors rise toward the top, the struts shorten, and their tails slide out over the trapezius / clavicle / upper back. ACROSS-BODY: the posterior strut lengthens over the back of the shoulder and the anterior one shortens. BEHIND-BACK: the anterior strut lengthens over the front of the shoulder and the posterior one shortens. All six hubs sit on stable skin (top/back/front of the scapula, or the arm saddle); only the struts cross the moving gap.
why_better: A topology with no hub on moving skin and no serial-wrist singularity. Its only singularity is coplanar n_i: cond(J) p98 is 5.7 on the clip frames for start set A. IK is trivial (d_i is an angle). All three active joints become muscle-like slides along arcs; for MVP2, a cable along each arc is the most natural remote drive. Compared with the baseline, the J2 hub (18 points of R1) and the free-form links that must clear every pose are replaced by narrow arcs on the paths the deltoid heads and their skin take.
main_risk: Three moving arcs cross the gap (3x the trombone's moving metal), with three tails. In the start set, strut lengths reach ~155 deg, which would wrap past the shoulder dome into the chest/neck; anchors with d_max <~120 deg are needed. Struts that cross each other need radial layers, +5 mm each. Workspace conditioning is poor (cond p98 48, |det| p2 0.04), and the anterior-medial anchor comes within 25 deg of the arm on the workspace. Reading the arm pose from three strut lengths needs forward kinematics (Newton on SO(3)). Six hubs.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm sets the three lengths, and every swivel and hinge follows by closure, so there is no spare. Rolling guides and v5 hubs. MVP2: each strut is driven like a muscle by a cable anchored at both strut ends over a capstan in its scapula guide. Sensing: a magnetic linear scale on each strut + a hall array in the guide; the arm orientation comes from forward kinematics on (d1, d2, d3) (2-3 Newton steps from the previous frame).

name: Skin-shaped offset arc + self-aligning cuff (non-spherical trombone)
topology: S -> J1: swivel about a line parallel to b, offset delta1 (<= 12 mm) from GH -> L1 guide -> J2: arc fixed to L2. The arc is a circle in 3-D whose axis line is parallel to p2 and passes delta2 (<= 15 mm) from GH; its radius is chosen to follow the skin rather than the GH sphere. It slides through the guide. -> L2 -> J3: O20 v5 hub about a line parallel to W, offset delta3 (<= 12 mm) -> the arm-side plate sits on a passive 3-slide self-aligning cuff stage (+-20 mm along the humerus, +-15 mm around the arm, +-4 mm radial, on rolling miniature guides) -> H (cuff). Active: J1, J2, J3. Passive: 3 cuff slides (outside the count, set by closure).
dof_reasoning: Composed rotations do not depend on where the axes sit, so the end orientation is rot(b,t1) rot(p2,t2) rot(W,t3), exactly as in the spherical chain. The three joint angles are therefore fixed by the arm's orientation (the same closure as trombone-arc). The axis offsets only translate the chain end by Delta(pose), and the three passive slides take up Delta, so their positions are also fixed by closure. These are the torque-free self-aligning cuff slides the user allows outside the count. No spare.
description: The trombone layout with the curvature freed. The band is a circle whose centre is not GH, so it can drop from ~48 mm over the top of the shoulder to ~60 mm over the deltoid instead of riding a single GH sphere. The swivel and hub axes can also sit where the skin wants them. The cost is a position error of up to ~15-20 mm, taken by a small slide stage between the J3 hub and BOTTOM on the cuff. REST / OVERHEAD / ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: metal positions as in trombone-arc (top swivel, band over the acromion to the lateral deltoid, tail over the trapezius overhead, over the scapula top across-body, over the clavicle region behind the back). The difference: the band follows a skin-shaped circle, and the cuff stage shifts up to 20 mm along and 15 mm around the arm.
why_better: It fixes the fundamental limit of rails: every point of a GH-centred rail is the same distance from GH, while the shoulder skin runs 37-76 mm from GH. It does so without adding an active DOF. The same slides also absorb the real GH translation relative to the scapula and the handler's ~15 mm skin slip (R10), which every spherical concept passes on to the skin. The bench cannot see this second benefit, because its GH is fixed in S.

The cuff stage adds ~8 mm of height and some mass on the arm, and must stay torque-free (R17: <= 5 N at the cuff), which calls for miniature rolling guides. The radial error must stay <= 4 mm or the liner gets squeezed. On the bench it looks like the trombone with extra metal. There are more parameters to fit.
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm sets the orientation and closure sets the slides; rolling slides avoid stick-slip. No spare. MVP2: as trombone-arc (J1 ring drum, a cable along the arc over a capstan in the guide, J3 hub drum). The slides stay passive and unsensed, because the joint angles alone give the arm orientation.

Per pose: HG = Rs.T @ Rh @ RH, the humerus in S (canonical axes humerus -y, lateral +z, anterior +x). A point x in S coordinates maps to thorax Rs@x; GH is the origin. Champion axes b = (-0.138,0.986,0.088), W0 = (0.079,-0.319,0.944), A1 77.41, A2 81.45 deg, branch -1. circ_int = band_impl.py line 892. Envelope fit on the fit clips. O20 v5 hub keep-out: r 10 mm, 12.25 mm stack.
ORIENTATION: W = HG@W0; p2 = circ_int(b, A1, W, A2, -1). Let F(u,v) = [u, normalize(v - (v.u) u), u x normalize(...)] (3x3 columns). Take a reference pose r (the first fit-clip frame) with p2_r, W_r, HG_r. Then R_L1 = F(b,p2) F(b,p2_r)^T; R_L2 = F(p2,W) F(p2_r,W_r)^T; R_H = HG HG_r^T, all in the S frame.
OFFSETS (design variables): o1 = a point on the J1 line (S); o2 = a point on the J2 line (reference coordinates); o3 = a point on the J3 line (reference coordinates).
TRANSFORMS: T_L1(x) = R_L1 (x - o1) + o1. T_L2(x) = T_L1(R12 (x - o2) + o2), with R12 = R_L1^T R_L2, a rotation about p2_r. T_E(x) = T_L2(R23 (x - o3) + o3), with R23 = R_L2^T R_H, a rotation about W_r. All metal is defined in reference coordinates and mapped by its member's transform; thorax = Rs @ T(x).
ARC: an L2-fixed circle about the J2 line: x(phi) = o2 + z_a p2_r + rho_a (cos phi e2_r + sin phi e3_r). Fit (o2, z_a, rho_a) by least squares to the pass-1 'skin + 6 mm' points along the trombone band path, in L2 reference coordinates; expect the circle centre 5-15 mm below/lateral of GH. Phi range as in trombone-arc (+-12 deg margin). Band 10 x 4 mm.
GUIDE: L1-fixed, at the arc point nearest the b direction in the reference pose; keep-out box 30 x 22 x 10 mm. The J1 ring is an annulus (radii 19-26 mm) around the J1 line, under the guide.
J3: O20 v5 hub on the J3 line at W_r. Its upper plate is on L2 (T_L2). Its lower plate sits on the CUFF STAGE, which moves with T_E: a 40 x 30 x 8 mm block of 3 stacked rolling slides. The stage's arm side is humerus-fixed at x_c (a reference point on the lateral arm under the hub); it maps by R_H (S coordinates), and then thorax = Rs @ R_H x_c.
SLIDES: Delta = T_E(x_c) - R_H x_c. In the humerus frame, Delta_H = R_H^T Delta, split into components along the humerus axis, tangential, and radial.
NOT TAKEN: closure fails; guide off the arc; |Delta_along| > 20 mm, |Delta_tan| > 15 mm or |Delta_rad| > 4 mm; any sample < 0 mm. Expect |Delta| up to ~2*10*sin 60 ~ 17 mm for 10 mm offsets.
GH translation: in use, the slides also absorb the real GH translation / R10 handler slip; this is not modelled on the bench.
sweep_params: Offsets delta1, delta3 (3-D, <= 12 mm). Arc circle: centre offset <= 15 mm, radius fitted to skin + 6 mm. Slide limits 15-25 / 10-20 / 3-5 mm. Axes and arc range as in trombone-arc.
prior_art: Stienen et al. 2009, self-aligning exoskeleton axes through decoupling of joint rotations and translations. In this repo: the P0 offset-axis minimax LP (pipeline/girdle/girdle.py) and the self-aligning 2R + ring + slider study (docs/P0_BASE_MOUNT.md section 8c).

name: Rolling-fin J2: strap-constrained spherical rolling cones on top of the scapula
topology: S -> J1: O20 v5 hub about b -> L1: hub upper plate + fin F1, a radial Ti fin 6 mm tall and 2.5 mm thick on a cone about u1 through GH (half-angle gamma1) -> J2: fin F2 on L2 (cone about u2, half-angle gamma2, with angle(u1,u2) = gamma1+gamma2) rolls on F1 without slip, held by two crossed 0.1 mm stainless flexure straps (figure-8) -> L2: F2 + strap to J3 -> J3: O20 v5 hub about W -> H. Active: J1, J2 (rolling coordinate phi), J3. Passive: none.
dof_reasoning: Rolling without slip couples the two cone rotations: L2 relative to L1 = rot(u1, phi) rot(u2, k phi), with k = sin gamma1 / sin gamma2. That is one coordinate, phi. Its instantaneous axis is the contact generator c (through GH), which travels along the fins. With J1 and J3 the chain has exactly 3 DOF: the arm pose fixes phi by a 1-D root, and then theta1 and theta3. The straps are structural (they prevent slip); they are not a transmission.
description: Two small curved walls stand on the stable top of the scapula, like the Risley turret's rings, and roll on each other as the arm moves. The contact point, and with it J2's axis, travels along the walls, so J2 is a joint with a moving axis. One strap runs from the moving fin down to the deltoid hub. REST: fins on the top, contact at one end of the fins, strap over the acromion to the lateral deltoid. OVERHEAD: the contact rolls to the other end, and the strap's root turns over the top. ACROSS-BODY / BEHIND-BACK: J1 turns the fin pair forward / backward, and the strap runs over the front / back of the shoulder. The fins are 6 mm tall, so J2 has no hub stack.
why_better: A 3R's middle axis is fixed in both of its links. That forces the closure band and the J2 placement trade-off: the Risley turret keeps J2 on the stable top, but only 59-70 % of the workspace closes. A rolling J2 has a moving middle axis: it is singular only when b, c(phi) and W are coplanar, and c moves with phi. It may therefore keep J2's metal on the stable top and still widen the closure band, with 6 mm fins instead of rings or hubs.
main_risk: The benefit is unproven: the moving axis has to actually widen the band, so test it first with a 50-design kinematic screen. Crossed flexure straps may count as 'cables' under the MVP1 rule (ask the user). IK needs a 1-D root find with several roots, so the solution can jump branches between frames. Slip/creep and strap fatigue. The fins are thin walls (pinch points, stiffness).
unpowered_and_mvp2: Unpowered: the arm sets the single rolling coordinate; rolling contact has near-zero friction. No spare. MVP2: drive J2 with a cable laid on F2's outer face (the fin is its own drum), or at a hub. Sensing: a magnetic pole strip on F1 read by a hall pair on F2 (phi); J1 and J3 by hub encoders.

REFERENCE: pose r = the first fit-clip frame. W_r = HG_r W0, and Y = HG HG_r^T per pose.

FORWARD: HG = rot(b,theta1) M(phi) rot(W_r,theta3) HG_r, with M(phi) = rot(u1_r,phi) rot(u2_r, k phi).
IK: f(phi) = b.(M(phi) W_r) - b.(Y W_r) on a 1 deg grid over [-180,180]. Find roots by sign change + bisection. Choose the root nearest the previous clip frame's phi (for ws poses, the root with the smallest |phi|). Then theta1 = atan2(b.(m x y), m.y - (b.m)(b.y)), with m = M W_r and y = Y W_r. R3 = (rot(b,theta1) M)^T Y must be a rotation about W_r (check |R3 W_r - W_r| < 1e-6); its angle is theta3.
CONTACT: c(phi) = rot(b,theta1) rot(u1_r,phi) c_r, with c_r = rot(m, gamma1) u1_r.
FINS: F1 (on L1) = {rot(b,theta1) r (cos gamma1 u1_r + sin gamma1 (cos a g1 + sin a g2))} for r in [R_f, R_f+6] and a in [a_c(phi_min)-6, a_c(phi_max)+6] deg, where a_c(phi) = a_c0 + phi is the contact azimuth about u1; 2.5 mm thick tangentially. F2 (on L2) = rot(b,theta1) M(phi) applied to the same form about u2_r, with an azimuth range of width k*(phi_max - phi_min) + 12 deg around the contact. Check that F2's contact sample coincides with c(phi) to fix the sign of the azimuth. R_f = envelope max under both fins + 2.
MEMBERS: the L1 plate = J1's upper plate + a 3 mm strap to F1's base. L2 = a strap from F2 to J3's upper plate (envelope fit). J1 and J3 are O20 v5 hubs at b and W as in trombone-arc, + BOTTOM stub.
NOT TAKEN: no root; phi outside the fin range; |det[b, c, W]| < 0.1; any sample < 0 mm.

name: Scapula halo track: J1 is a closed cam track on low-motion scapula skin and the J2 hub rides it
topology: Scapula base (S): a closed halo track T fixed to the handler, bent along an iso-motion contour of the scapula-frame skin around the acromion summit. It runs low over the supraspinatus and scapular spine at the back and climbs over the acromion laterally and anteriorly. -> J1 ACTIVE: a bogie carriage on T. Its coordinate s (position along the track) is the joint value, so J1 is a 1-DOF spherical joint whose path is non-circular. The carriage frame is [u(s), track tangent, normal]. -> J2 ACTIVE: an O20 hub on the carriage. Its axis is p2 = u(s), the radial direction from GH through the carriage. -> link 2: a strap, arc a2 (55-115 deg). -> J3 ACTIVE: an O20 hub at W, fixed to the arm on skin a hub can sit on (deltoid cap, delta 75-115 from the down-the-arm axis). -> arm-end plate + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning:
There are three coordinates (s, q2, q3), each a real joint that the arm drives and a sensor reads. Given the arm orientation, w = RH W fixes s through angle(u(s), w) = a2, a 1-D root that is transversal by design, so the carriage is pinned. q2 is the azimuth of w about p2, measured from the track tangent. q3 is the remaining twist about w. Nothing is left free and nothing can sag (R17).

A closed track gives s unlimited travel. Every spherical 3R needs that over the functional workspace. I computed, over the 1788 bench poses, that the smallest possible J1 span is about 172 deg, and then J3 must turn about 290 deg (or the other way round). J1 and J3 must turn almost all the way round, and a hub or a closed track can do that.
description:
Rest:
- A Ti ring (8 x 5 mm section, about 240 mm long, about 50 g) rides 2-5 mm over the top of the shoulder on skin fixed to the scapula.
- In the scapula frame it sits at el about 15-35 deg at the back over the spine and supraspinatus (55-60 mm from GH), el about 40-55 laterally over the acromion, el about 60-75 at the front over the anterior acromion and clavicle, and el about 80 medially near the summit.
- Over the fit clips this skin moves at most 13-20 mm against the scapula, and at most 5 mm over most of the ring.
- The carriage and the J2 hub sit in the posterior or posterolateral sector. A short link 2 (55-65 deg when W is at the proximity agent's low-motion spot, about (112, -15)) reaches the J3 hub on the top-lateral deltoid just below the acromion edge.

Other poses (from a kinematic screen with a sample loop):
- Overhead: the crossing stays posterior (ring azimuth -40..+25).
- Reaching forward or across the body: the carriage runs to the posterolateral sector (az 15-70) and link 2 passes over the posterior and lateral deltoid.
- Behind the back: the zone-boundary loop has no crossing. This is the known range hole; a loop extended further anteriorly or inferiorly, or W moved anteriorly, may close it.

No metal ever sits between the arm and the trunk.
why_better:
It removes the J2 problem at its root:
- The baseline's J2 pole sweeps a circle 77 deg from J1 over skin that moves a median 29 mm (p90 71 mm) against the scapula. I computed this from the r18 chain and the skin-motion map. That zone alone costs 18 points of R1 and is 'unfixable by shape' (docs/research/proximity_levers.md).
- Here J2 can only be where the track is, and the track is drawn on skin that moves at most 13-20 mm. The J2 hub, the carriage and the track are therefore in band by construction, and the J1 hub disappears.

It also escapes a conflict I measured:
- If both end hubs must sit on skin a hub can sit on (radial ray within 30 deg of the skin normal, motion at most 15-25 mm, within 120 mm), the best singularity margin of ANY spherical 3R over the functional workspace is only 15-17 deg. A track has no pole to place.

First kinematic screen (unoptimised zone-boundary loops, transversal crossing required):
- 13 mm contour loop, W (115, -18), a2 55: closes 67 % of the workspace and 94 % of clip frames. Link 2 is short and J3 sits on the best arm spot.
- 20 mm contour loop, W (75, 54), a2 115: closes 88.5 % and 95 %.
main_risk:
- Reach against track placement: the loop that stays on the best skin closes only 59-67 % of the workspace (behind-back has no crossing). The 20 mm loop reaches 88 %, but link 2 becomes long (115 deg) over the deltoid.
- Near-tangent crossings are singular: two roots close together, as at rest. There the carriage speeds up, and unpowered the arm can push the carriage across the track (transmission angle, R17).
- A non-circular track needs a bogie carriage (2 roller pairs about 15 mm apart) with some play at changes of curvature.
- The user's handler must carry a ring around the acromion.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered:
- The closure pins the carriage. With a transversal crossing the arm drives it like any joint.
- The bogie runs on 4 small rollers (MR63) on a hard-faced Ti track. J2 and J3 are preloaded O20 pairs.
- R17 check: report the transmission factor ds/dtheta and keep |d angle/ds| >= 0.5 deg per 3 deg of track.

MVP2:
- The carriage is a natural cable joint: a cable pair anchored at the carriage runs in a groove along the track to the remote motor, a linear pull on a closed track.
- s is read by a magnetic linear scale on the track.
- J2 and J3 are hubs with cable drums.

COMMON KIT (identical in every spec)

K0 Setup. import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools'); import concept_bench as CB; B=CB.Bench(60,160). Use the fast grid cache if it is built (python3 tools/concept_bench.py --build 60 160).
- Pose i: RS=B.frames(i)['S'][0], RH=B.frames(i)['H'][0], GH = origin. S and H have zero translation; the trunk moves by -lift.
- A scapula-frame direction u maps to RS@u; a humerus-frame direction maps to RH@u.
- bvec(az,el)=[-cos el cos az, sin el, cos el sin az] (scapula frame: az 0 posterior, 90 lateral, 180 anterior, -90 medial).
- wdir(d,a)=[sin d sin a, -cos d, sin d cos a] (humerus frame: d from the down-the-arm axis; a 0 lateral, +90 anterior, -90 posterior).
- These match band_impl.bvec and w_dir.

K1 Two-circle closure.
- c=b.w, n=(b x w)/|b x w|.
- A=(cos a1 - c cos a2)/(1-c^2), Bq=(cos a2 - c cos a1)/(1-c^2).
- p0=A b+Bq w, h2=1-|p0|^2. If h2<=0 there is no closure -> None.
- p2=p0+sigma*sqrt(h2)*n, with sigma=+-1 fixed per design.
- margin=min(theta-|a1-a2|, a1+a2-theta, 360-a1-a2-theta), theta=acos c. margin<5 deg -> None.

K2 Continuity. Walk B.clip_order(). A clip frame whose joint values jump more than 25 deg from the previous taken frame is a branch flip -> None.

K3 Rigid skin-fitted underside.
- A member is a set of unit directions u_j in its own frame, spaced 2 mm at its height and across its width.
- Per pose, the requirement r_i(d) = the first t on a 1 mm march (15-220 mm) along d with B.dist(i, t d) >= 2.0 and >= 0 over [t, t+15]. Vectorise over all samples.
- rho_j = quantile_q over the fit poses of r_i(R_member,i u_j). Fit poses = all poses the chain closes in, clip and ws. q=1.0 by default; q=0.97 or 0.93 lets the worst poses become contact poses.
- Metal = rho_j R_member u_j. B.dist then decides contact.

K4 O20 hub (docs/HARDWARE.md v5).
- A flat disc of radius 10 mm perpendicular to its axis k, lower face at distance h_F along k.
- h_F = max over the disc samples (2 mm grid) and fit poses of the K3 requirement projected on k.
- The skin-facing samples are the disc.
- Lower member [F, F+3]; upper member underside at F+3.15; crown at F+12.25.

K5 Strap. 12 mm wide, 3 mm thick (report mass at 5.5 mm too), K3 underside. It may not climb faster than 60 deg from the plane of the hub it leaves.

K6 Collisions.
- Each member is its samples with radial intervals [rho, rho+t].
- Two members that do not share a joint collide if two samples are within (half-widths+1 mm)/rho rad and their intervals overlap (+0.5 mm).
- Joint partners are exempt within hub radius+2 mm of their joint.
- Collision -> None.

K7 Neck and record.
- Neck: a 14 x 6 mm strap from the arm-end plate to BOTTOM's bar. In the humerus frame the bar normal is Wb=(0,-0.0713,0.9975), its underside is 67.5 mm out along Wb, and it runs along Db=(0,-0.9975,-0.0713) from about 40 mm down. Fit with K3 in RH.
- B.record(i, all custom metal samples). That is everything except the user's cuff and BOTTOM.
- Print B.report(), the in-band share per member (B.dist per member) and the Ti mass (4.43 g/cm3).

SPECIFIC

Track:
- First version: for each scapula azimuth az (-180..180, step 3), find el*(az) = the lowest elevation above which every cell of pipeline/conformal/analysis/skin_motion_map_14.json ['scapula']['grid'] (grid axes a = az, b = el, 'motion' in mm) has 0 <= motion <= thr (thr 13 or 20).
- Smooth el* with a 9-tap circular mean and add 4 deg. The seed for thr 13 is el+4 = posterior 15-39, lateral 48, anterior 58-74, medial 76-86.
- u(az) = bvec(az, el*); 120 samples.
- Later version: a 3-harmonic Fourier perturbation of el*(az).
- Track running radius per sample: rho_T,j = (K3 requirement in RS) + 5. The 8 mm wide underside at rho_T - 5 is the skin-facing metal.

Closure per pose:
- w = RH W; Ut = RS u(az); f(az) = angle(Ut, w) - a2.
- Roots are sign changes of f; refine linearly.
- Require >= 2 roots and |delta f| >= 0.5 deg per sample at the chosen root, else None.
- Branch: the root where sign((Ut x dUt/daz).w) = sigma. Continuity per K2.

Carriage:
- A 20 x 16 mm block, radial extent [rho_T - 5, rho_T + 4].
- The J2 hub is K4 with axis p2 = Ut(root). Its lower member is the carriage: F2 = rho_T + 4.
- q2 = azimuth of w about p2 from the track tangent.

Link 2:
- A strap along the great circle p2 -> w (arc a2) in the frame [p2, e, p2 x e], e = norm(w - (w.p2) p2).
- K3 underside, ramp-limited from F2+3.15 and from the J3 plane.

J3 and arm end:
- K4 hub with axis w. The arm-end plate (fixed in RH, K3) is the lower member and link 2 the upper; sweep the reverse order too.
- Neck to BOTTOM per K7.

Collisions (K6): link 2 may pass over the track only above rho_T + 4.5; also carriage vs J3, and neck vs link 2.

Report the closure share alongside the bench metrics.
sweep_params:
- Track: thr 8/13/20 contour, el offset 0-8 deg, or 3-harmonic Fourier coefficients around it.
- W: delta 75-115, az -40..55.
- a2: 45-120 deg.
- Branch sigma.
- Envelope quantile q: 1.0 / 0.97 / 0.93.
- Stacking order at J3.
prior_art:
Closest:
- Curved guide rails with bogie carriages (HepcoMotion and THK track systems; roller-coaster bogies).
- Circular arc guides in shoulder and upper-arm exos (e.g. the curved guide of Gopura & Kiguchi's SUEFUL-7) and RCM arc guides in surgical robots. All of these are circular.

I know of no device with a non-circular spherical track drawn on the skin that sets the locus of the chain's middle joint.

name: Deltoid oval track: J3 is a closed cam track fixed to the arm, carrying the J2 hub (mirror of the halo track)
topology: Scapula base (S) -> J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis b on the lateral acromion top. b = bvec(106, 64) in the scapula frame: the radial ray is within 30 deg of the skin normal there, and the skin moves at most 15 mm. -> link 1: a strap with arc a1 of about 70 deg. -> J2 ACTIVE: an O20 hub on a carriage. Its axis p2 is the radial direction through the carriage, with angle(b, p2) = a1. -> J3 ACTIVE: the carriage runs on a closed oval track fixed to the arm on the deltoid cap. The oval is centred at delta 95 / az -10 with semi-axes of 30 deg in delta and 60 deg in az. Its coordinate t is the joint value. -> The oval is the arm end and merges with BOTTOM's top and neck.
dof_reasoning:
There are three coordinates (q1, q2, t), all driven by the arm and all sensable.
- The closure fixes t: the circle at angle a1 about b, mapped into the humerus frame, must cross the oval transversally. That is a 1-D root along the oval.
- q1 is the azimuth of the crossing about b.
- q2 is the twist about p2 between link 1 and the carriage frame (oval tangent).

No coordinate is free. The closed oval gives t unlimited travel, which suits the end joint that has to turn about 290 deg.
description:
Rest:
- A racetrack ring of about 60 x 125 mm (track 8 x 5 mm, about 310 mm long, about 65 g Ti) lies 2-5 mm over the lateral deltoid cap, fixed to the arm and joined to BOTTOM's top.
- It reaches from just under the acromion edge (delta about 125) down to the deltoid belly (delta about 65), and from the posterolateral to the anterolateral cap.
- The J1 hub sits on the top of the lateral acromion. A 70 deg link 1 runs down over the acromion edge to the carriage and J2 hub on the oval.

Overhead: the oval rotates up with the arm and the carriage slides toward the part of the oval nearest the acromion, so link 1 stays short over the top. Across-body and behind-back: the carriage runs to the anterior or posterior end of the oval. No link 2, no J3 hub, no separate neck.
why_better:
It deletes the arm end that hurts the baseline:
- The J3 hub plus neck (17 pts of R1).
- Link 2's ribbon (16 pts).
- The link-2-vs-neck interference, which is the only part collision left in the r20 picks (FINDINGS).

The only member that moves against both frames is link 1, from the acromion top. The long member is fixed to the arm and shaped over the arm skin in the humerus frame.

Kinematic screen (unoptimised oval, transversal crossing): b = bvec(106, 64), a1 = 70 closes 84.5 % of the functional workspace and 100 % of clip frames. J1 is on skin a hub can sit on, which the best 3R layouts cannot manage at that margin.
main_risk:
- Arm skin under a part fixed to the arm still moves 11-25 mm over the clips (the best arm spot moves 11-12 mm), and the oval's posterior end reaches skin that moves 36-50 mm. Its in-band ceiling is therefore lower than the scapula halo's.
- The top of the oval goes under the acromion edge at elevation, where the deltoid bunches: contact and squeeze risk.
- A long track adds mass on the arm, inertia that the arm must carry.
- Near-tangent crossings: same singularity issue as the halo track.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: the bogie carriage is pinned by the closure; rolling rollers; the J1 and J2 O20 hubs are preloaded. Nothing is free.

MVP2: a cable runs along the oval's groove from a remote motor (the Bowden sheath crosses the shoulder like any cable), with a magnetic strip for t. J1 and J2 have hub drums.

- Link 2 = the carriage + a 15 mm bridge to J3's upper plate.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub at W, fixed to the arm on a deltoid-cap spot a hub can sit on (delta 75-115, e.g. the low-motion spot (112, -15)).

- The J1 hub sits on the lateral or posterior acromion. Link 1 is a short strap to a curved rail: 140-190 deg of a circle of radius about 45-55 mm about the J2 axis, section 8 x 5 mm.
- The rail lies over the deltoid cap and posterior shoulder, about 60-65 mm from GH.
- The carriage sits next to the J3 hub on the top-lateral deltoid. There is no metal at J2's pole.

Overhead: the rail on link 1 swings with q1 over the shoulder top while the carriage runs along it; the arm-end hub stays on the deltoid cap. Across-body and behind-back: the carriage reaches the rail's ends (the extremes of the J2 angle).

It deletes the baseline's two worst members at once:
- The J2 hub zone: 18.4 pts of R1 lost, 0.7 % in band, and unfixable by shape.
- Link 2's ribbon: 16.1 pts.

Link 2 becomes a 20 mm carriage next to the arm-end hub, which sits on the best arm spot. The rail is a thin band at constant radius. Where it lies over the round deltoid cap (radius spread about 4.7 mm), it stays in band at any rotation. The arcs and axes stay those of a proven 3R, so the comparison with the baseline isolates the J2 realisation.
main_risk:
- J2 travel: the J2 angle spans 94 deg on the clips but 159 deg over the functional workspace for the r18 chain (17-176 deg). For the layouts with the best singularity margin it spans 119-133 deg (computed).
- The rail is therefore a 140-190 deg arc plus carriage on link 1: long intermediate metal that swings with q1 and must clear the arm and the acromion in every pose.
- At constant radius it stands off where the skin under it is not the deltoid cap.
- Its free ends are cantilevers (stiffness).
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: a rolling carriage (4 MR63 V-rollers on a V-edged Ti rail, or a caged wire-race segment). J2 has no hub friction and nothing is free.

MVP2: a cable groove along the rail (a pull along the arc) drives the carriage, with a magnetic strip for q2. J1 and J3 are hubs with drums.

name: Rolling-cone elbow: J2 is a pair of strap-bound cones rolling about GH, with no hub
topology:
- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub, axis b.
- Link 1 ends in a 'sun' conical rim: axis s fixed in link 1, half-angle alpha1, apex at GH.
- J2 ACTIVE: no-slip rolling contact with link 2's 'planet' conical rim (axis c, half-angle alpha2, external contact angle(s, c) = alpha1 + alpha2). Two or three crossed 0.1 mm steel straps hold the pair together, Jacob's-ladder style. It is a 1-DOF spherical joint whose instantaneous axis is the contact generator through GH.
- Link 2.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub at W (deltoid cap, delta 75-115).
- Arm-end plate + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning:
There are three coordinates (q1, rolling angle psi, q3).
- The rolling pair has exactly one DOF (no slip + contact + straps); the straps add no DOF.
- Its relative motion is M(psi) = R(s, psi) R(c0, k psi) with k = sin(alpha1)/sin(alpha2): a rotation about the moving contact line through GH. The chain therefore stays spherical about GH.
- The arm's three orientation DOF fix (q1, psi, q3) through a 1-D root in psi. No spare coordinate.
description:
Rest: the J1 hub sits on the acromion. Link 1 runs to a standing curved rim (an 8 mm tall, 2 mm thick conical band, radially oriented, 60-90 mm long) over the posterior-lateral shoulder. Link 2's rim rolls on it and link 2 continues to the J3 hub on the deltoid cap. The chain's 'elbow' is two thin rims touching along a radial line: no hub, no cap.

Overhead and across-body: the planet rim rolls along the sun rim. Each rim needs only about half the arc that a rail of the same J2 travel would, because both surfaces move.
why_better:
- It removes the 12.25 mm J2 hub stack and its 20 mm disc, the baseline's worst zone (18 pts of R1, 0.7 % in band). - Rolling contact has near-zero friction (R17) and no bearing play.
- Because the elbow's axis migrates, the chain's singularity set is not the 3R's coplanarity set. This is a new place to put the singularity.
main_risk:
- Novel and fiddly. The cones must stay in contact under every load direction: straps take tension one way and contact the other, so it needs crossed straps on both sides plus preload.
- The rims stand 8 mm radially and still need skin clearance.
- Slip under load would corrupt the angle reading.
- Fatigue of 0.1 mm straps over 10^6 cycles.
- The singularity map has to be built from scratch.
- Sensing psi needs an encoder on the rolling pair.

name: Open-centre ring joints: all three joints as thin-section rings around their poles, so bumps rise into the hole

- Scapula base (S).
- J1 ACTIVE: a thin-section ring bearing (wire-race or Kaydon KAA-type, mean radius r_m 14-24 mm, 5 x 5 mm section), concentric with axis b and lying on the sphere around b's pole with an open centre. The inner race is the lower member and the outer race the upper member, at the same height.

- J2 ACTIVE: a ring about p2.
- Link 2.
- J3 ACTIVE: a ring about W (arm-fixed).
- Arm-end + neck to BOTTOM.

Rest:
- Three rings of 30-50 mm, each a 5 mm-tall annulus around its pole.
- J1's ring circles the acromion summit, so the bony peak sits inside the open centre.
- J3's ring circles the most bulging point of the deltoid cap, so the bulge rises into the centre when the deltoid fires.
- The links are short straps between ring rims. There is no pin and no dome cap anywhere.

It attacks the hub directly.
- The O20 stack is 12.25 mm from the lower face to the crown, and its flat face must clear the highest skin under it.
- A ring's skin-facing metal is an annulus with an axisymmetric underside that follows the skin, and the local bump (acromion summit, deltoid belly) can rise into its open centre. Its crown is about 9 mm.
- The lower crown reduces the link-over-hub and link-vs-hub collisions that cost the stacked designs range.
- It tests a claim directly: 'joints on bumps should be rings, not discs'.
main_risk:
- Larger footprint: OD 35-48 mm against 20 mm. The evaluator found that a larger hub radius costs about 20 points of workspace (O17 vs O23), because flat discs ride high on curved skin. The ring must win that back with its axisymmetric open annulus, or it loses.
- Mass: 6-18 g per ring. A preloaded thin-section ring needs a stiff housing, and the housing sets the real stack.
- A cable drum on a 48 mm ring is large. Torque is not the problem: for MVP2's ~10 N.m, a KAA15 ring has a 40 N.m static moment rating.
unpowered_and_mvp2:
Unpowered: four-point-contact thin-section rings, friction about 0.1 N.m (ring_and_shell_hardware.md); nothing is free.

MVP2: the outer race carries the cable groove. At a pitch radius of about 24 mm the cable sees about 420 N at 10 N.m, less than the O20's 950 N. Sensing is a thin magnetic ring encoder in the race.

- Scapula base (S), low on the infraspinatus.
- J1 ACTIVE: O20 hub with a wedge or skin-normal seat, axis b = bvec(-28, -19) (posterior-inferior-medial).
- Link 1: a 90 deg strap up the back of the scapula.
- J2 ACTIVE: O20 hub at the common perpendicular, p2 = +(b x w)/|b x w|. On this branch it rides the posterior-superior shoulder: scapula-frame az 45-60, el 30-40, about 50 mm from GH.
- Link 2: a 90 deg strap down the posterior deltoid.
- J3 ACTIVE: O20 hub with a wedge seat, W = wdir(42, -64) on the posterior upper arm.
- Arm-end + neck to BOTTOM.
dof_reasoning:
A spherical 3R with a1 = a2 = 90 (a Cardan). p2 = sigma (b x w)/|b x w| in closed form, q2 = theta = angle(b, w), and q1, q3 follow; there is no spare coordinate.

For any spherical 3R the best possible singularity margin over the arcs is reached at 90/90, and then it equals the distance of w from the line b. This placement maximises it over the whole functional workspace: 32.6-34.6 deg (computed over the bench poses, Fibonacci search over b and W). The baseline has a 13 deg fold margin and 3.2 % of the workspace beyond its extended singularity.
description:
Everything sits behind the frontal plane:
- J1 is low on the back of the scapula, 119-135 mm from GH.
- Link 1 runs up the infraspinatus to J2 on the posterior acromion and scapular spine. Under J2 the scapula-frame skin moves a median of 10 mm (p90 38-49 mm), against 29 mm (p90 71 mm) for the baseline's J2.
- Link 2 runs down the posterior deltoid to J3 on the posterior upper arm, 109-125 mm from GH.

The front and top of the shoulder are empty: overhead and across-body, nothing is in front of or above the acromion. Reaching behind the back, the arm swings toward the chain (the main risk).

It is range-first by construction:
- It is the global optimum of the singularity margin for any spherical 3R over the bench's functional workspace. Kinematic closure is 100 %, with theta 30-149 deg.
- Its J2 pole lives over the low-motion posterior-superior scapula skin.

- At both end poles the radial rays meet the skin about 49 deg off the normal (back of the scapula, posterior arm), 110-135 mm from GH. J1 and J3 therefore need wedge or tilted seats that add stack.
- If hubs are restricted to skin within 30 deg of the normal and moving at most 15-25 mm, the best margin drops to 15-17 deg (computed).

- Long links, about 150 mm each.
- Posterior arm skin moves 26-58 mm in the humerus frame: bad ground for J3.
- Behind-back reaches squeeze link 2 between the arm and the back.

MVP2: cables to three hubs. J1 on the back is the shortest cable route to a motor pack worn on the back.

- c=b.w, n=(b x w)/|b x w|.
- A=(cos a1 - c cos a2)/(1-c^2), Bq=(cos a2 - c cos a1)/(1-c^2).
- p0=A b+Bq w, h2=1-|p0|^2. If h2<=0 there is no closure -> None.
- p2=p0+sigma*sqrt(h2)*n, with sigma=+-1 fixed per design.
- margin=min(theta-|a1-a2|, a1+a2-theta, 360-a1-a2-theta), theta=acos c. margin<5 deg -> None.

K2 Continuity. Walk B.clip_order(). A clip frame whose joint values jump more than 25 deg from the previous taken frame is a branch flip -> None.

K3 Rigid skin-fitted underside.
- A member is a set of unit directions u_j in its own frame, spaced 2 mm at its height and across its width.
- Per pose, the requirement r_i(d) = the first t on a 1 mm march (15-220 mm) along d with B.dist(i, t d) >= 2.0 and >= 0 over [t, t+15]. Vectorise over all samples.
- rho_j = quantile_q over the fit poses of r_i(R_member,i u_j). Fit poses = all poses the chain closes in, clip and ws. q=1.0 by default; q=0.97 or 0.93 lets the worst poses become contact poses.
- Metal = rho_j R_member u_j. B.dist then decides contact.

K4 O20 hub (docs/HARDWARE.md v5).
- A flat disc of radius 10 mm perpendicular to its axis k, lower face at distance h_F along k.
- h_F = max over the disc samples (2 mm grid) and fit poses of the K3 requirement projected on k.
- The skin-facing samples are the disc.
- Lower member [F, F+3]; upper member underside at F+3.15; crown at F+12.25.

K5 Strap. 12 mm wide, 3 mm thick (report mass at 5.5 mm too), K3 underside. It may not climb faster than 60 deg from the plane of the hub it leaves.

K6 Collisions.
- Each member is its samples with radial intervals [rho, rho+t].
- Two members that do not share a joint collide if two samples are within (half-widths+1 mm)/rho rad and their intervals overlap (+0.5 mm).
- Joint partners are exempt within hub radius+2 mm of their joint.
- Collision -> None.
